doc.headline: Atlas-L is the best on overall quality in every task but costs {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} per 1k conversations; Brisk-S costs {cost_per_1k.brisk-s} and is weakest on quality. Which to buy is the owner's price.
doc.lede: Nothing was declared in advance, so no option fails a gate and none dominates. Quality falls and cost falls together as you move down from Atlas-L, except Open-70B, which beats Brisk-S on quality in some tasks at about twice its cost.

caveats.material_if: an owner declares a quality floor or a price per quality point; the ranking would then follow that rule, which could pick a different arm.
a claim that one arm beats another is read from the intervals alone, which are unpaired here.
the judge favours one arm's style on the judged aspects; the cost figures do not rest on it.
the pick leads by little; with four arms a re-run would likely read the leader lower.

decision.text: Moving from Atlas-L to Brisk-S cuts cost per 1k conversations from {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} to {cost_per_1k.brisk-s} and loses overall quality in every task, most in troubleshooting ({task.trouble.atlas-l.overall.mean} against {task.trouble.brisk-s.overall.mean}).

Atlas-M ({cost_per_1k.atlas-m}) and Open-70B ({cost_per_1k.open-70b}) sit between; Open-70B matches Atlas-M on persona ({task.persona.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.persona.atlas-m.overall.mean}) at a lower cost, but trails it on research ({task.research.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.research.atlas-m.overall.mean}).

Our lean, not a rule: Atlas-M as the general option, since it stays within a few points of Atlas-L at well under half its cost. It holds for any owner who values a point of quality at more than the price gap.
A declared price per quality point or a quality floor, and a paired re-run of the finalists on the same cases.

doc.flag: Costs are this run's provider routing's, not the models' own: no arm names who served it. No gate, floor or price per quality point was declared, so this is a trade for the owner to price, not a recommendation.
doc.headline: Atlas-L scores highest on overall quality in every task but costs the most ({cost_per_1k.atlas-l} per 1k conversations); Brisk-S costs {cost_per_1k.brisk-s}. The choice is the owner's price, at an unknown provider routing.
doc.lede: Quality and cost fall together down the Atlas line. Open-70B sits between on cost ({cost_per_1k.open-70b}) but is weak at confirming before account changes ({task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean}, against {task.trouble.atlas-l.confirms.mean} for Atlas-L).

caveats.material_if: an owner declares a quality floor or a price per quality point; the ranking would then follow that rule and could pick a different arm.
a gap between two arms is read from their own unpaired intervals; the gaps between neighbouring arms in a task are within a few points and may not be separated.
the judge favours one arm's style on the per-aspect judged figures; the cost figures do not rest on it.

Atlas-L's slim point-estimate leads in speculation and persona are the best of four arms; a re-run on fresh cases would likely read them lower. Its larger leads in troubleshooting and research do not rest on this.

decision.text: Moving from Atlas-L to Brisk-S cuts cost per 1k conversations from {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} to {cost_per_1k.brisk-s} at this routing, and loses overall quality in every task, most in troubleshooting ({task.trouble.atlas-l.overall.mean} against {task.trouble.brisk-s.overall.mean}).

Atlas-M ({cost_per_1k.atlas-m}) is {task.trouble.atlas-l.overall.mean} against {task.trouble.atlas-m.overall.mean} behind Atlas-L in troubleshooting. Open-70B ({cost_per_1k.open-70b}) is above Atlas-M on persona ({task.persona.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.persona.atlas-m.overall.mean}) but below it on research ({task.research.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.research.atlas-m.overall.mean}) and billing. Which of these is worth its price depends on a price per quality point nobody declared.

The cheapest arms are weakest at confirming before account changes: Open-70B {task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean} and Brisk-S {task.trouble.brisk-s.confirms.mean}, against {task.trouble.atlas-m.confirms.mean} for the Atlas arms. That is an account-safety cost the overall score hides.
The owner of the assistant declares a price per quality point or a quality floor (including one for confirming before account changes), and states which provider serves each model.

claims.text: Atlas-L has the highest overall quality in every task by point estimate; it is clearly separated from every other arm in billing, troubleshooting and research, but not from Atlas-M in speculation or from Open-70B in persona.

evidence.caption: Overall quality by task and arm, with intervals at the stated level, unpaired.

claims.text: Brisk-S is lowest on overall quality in troubleshooting, persona and speculation; Open-70B is lowest in billing and, by a margin the intervals nearly overlap, research.

evidence.caption: The two cheapest arms' overall quality by task.

claims.text: Cost per 1k conversations runs from {cost_per_1k.atlas-l} for Atlas-L down to {cost_per_1k.brisk-s} for Brisk-S, and the order is the same in every task; this is the cost at this run's unnamed provider routing.

claims.text: Open-70B and Brisk-S confirm before account changes less often in troubleshooting than the Atlas arms, which is what a cheaper arm would give up.
